name: fixedheap-small
algorithm: The task of tests/bench/idiomatic/alloc-small: a ring of 4,096 live objects of 8 to 256 bytes (sizes and contents from splitmix64), each step reading the oldest, allocating and filling a new one, then freeing the old; the Mk cell allocates from std.mem.FixedHeap over a 2 MiB buffer, every other cell from its language's general-purpose allocator; the wrapping sum of each object's length, first and last byte (../README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; allocation has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: an idiomatic row compares allocators; every column makes the same objects in the same order, and the checksum reads every object once
notes: Allocators named: mk std.mem.FixedHeap over a 2 MiB buffer taken once from the program's arena (HeapList[u8] objects, and the ring in the same FixedHeap); c malloc and free of the static UCRT; rust System (HeapAlloc); zig std.heap.smp_allocator; go the garbage-collected runtime allocator (GOGC=100, labelled: it frees in batches).

No standard library of the four has an allocator over a caller's buffer that frees and reuses any block, so the other cells are alloc-small's: the same task through each general-purpose allocator. Read beside tests/bench/idiomatic/alloc-small, whose mk cell is std's general heap.
